newsitem.title: GERMANY: E-Plus offers longer contracts at lower rates.
newsitem.headline: E-Plus offers longer contracts at lower rates.

text.p: E-Plus Mobilfunk GmbH, the mobile phone company, on Friday stepped up the pace in Germany's latest price war for mobile communications services by offering sharply lower monthly charges for long-term contracts.

From November 4 E-Plus will offer a new "Partner Plus" tariff with a monthly basic charge of 19.95 marks ($12.93) and one-off connection charges of 99 marks. Calling rates per minute for the package are 1.79 marks peak time and 39 pfennigs off-peak.
For calls within the E-Plus network, calling charges will be 59 pfennigs peak and 29 pfennigs.
New subscribers must sign a two-year contract to take advantage of the new rates.

A second new tariff package aimed at professional customers called "Profi Plus" will carry a monthly charge of 59.95 marks and a one-off connection fee of 99 marks. Calling rates will be 89 pfennigs per minute in peak times and 59 pfennigs per minute in off-peak.
For calls within the E-Plus network, from one E-Plus subscriber to another, rates will be 59 pfennigs peak and 29 pfennigs off-peak.
The contracts carry a minimum duration of two years. There is also a monthly minimum usage for each package of 20 marks and 10 marks respectively.
Herbert Brehnke, managing director of E-Plus, said the new tariffs were the cheapest available in Germany.
"The new development in prices on the mobile communications market will lead consumers to think things over again. Using mobile phones has become affordable," he said in a statement.
E-Plus will continue to offer its two previous tariff packages, Partner and Profi, which carry a monthly charge of 44 marks and 59 marks and a commitment of 12 months and six months respectively.
Subscribers who switch from one of the old tariff packages to a new one will pay a one-off fee ranging from 28 marks to 199 marks, depending on how long they have held their existing contract.
E-Plus is owned by energy group Veba AG, steel and engineering firm Thyssen AG, BellSouth of the United States and British mobile phone groiup Vodafone.

The change in E-Plus tariffs is the latest round in a mobile phone price war sparked by Deutsche Telekom AG last week. Telekom stunned its main competitors by slashing the monthly charge for its D1 network to 29 marks from 49 marks.

Mannesmann Mobilfunk followed suit earlier this week, saying it would cut charges on a peak call on its D2-Classic package by 30 pfennigs to 99 pfennigs a minute, while leaving connection charges and monthly fees unchanged at 99 marks and 69.95 marks respectively.

It also said it was halving the monthly rental on its D2-Fun deal to 24.95 marks, leaving call charges unchanged at 1.89 marks peak rate and 39 pfennigs off-peak. The basic connection fee remains unchanged at 99 marks.
-- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 26097150 ($ = 1.541 German Marks)
